{{Short description|Mathematical finite group theory}}
In mathematical [[finite group|finite]] [[group theory]], the '''classical involution theorem''' of {{harvs|txt|last=Aschbacher|year1=1977a|year2=1977b|year3=1980}} classifies [[simple group]]s with a classical [[Involution (mathematics)|involution]] and satisfying some other conditions, showing that they are mostly [[group of Lie type|groups of Lie type]] over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] of odd [[field characteristic|characteristic]]. {{harvtxt|Berkman|2001}} extended the classical involution theorem to [[groups of finite Morley rank]].

A '''classical involution''' ''t'' of a finite group ''G'' is an involution whose centralizer has a [[subnormal subgroup]] containing ''t'' with quaternion [[Sylow theorems|Sylow 2-subgroups]].
